The database schema named 'rschema_0382' contains three tables: User, Post, and User_post_comment.
The User table represents a user in the social media platform. It has seven columns: Age, Gender, Interests, Name, Occupation, Password, Personal_profile, and User_ID. User_ID is the primary key, and it is an integer. The User table stores information about the user such as their age, gender, interests, name, occupation, password, and personal profile.
The Post table is another table in the schema. It has four columns: Description, Image_URL, Post_ID, Title, and User_ID. Post_ID is the primary key, and it is an integer. User_ID is a foreign key referencing the User table, indicating which user created the post. The Post table stores information about the post such as its description, image URL, title, and the user who created it.
The User_post_comment table is a junction table that connects the User and Post tables. It has four columns: Comment_content, Comment_time, Post_ID, and User_ID. Post_ID and User_ID are foreign keys referencing the Post and User tables respectively. The primary key of this table is a combination of User_ID, Post_ID, and Comment_time. The User_post_comment table stores information about the comments made by users on posts.
The User table allows null values for the Gender and Interests columns, but it does not allow null values for the Name, Occupation, Password, Personal_profile, and Username columns. If a user does not provide these details, they will be prompted to do so.
The User_post_comment table has foreign key references to both the User and Post tables, ensuring referential integrity. If a user or post is deleted, the corresponding entries in the User_post_comment table will be automatically deleted to maintain data consistency. The DELETE rule is set to CASCADE, meaning that if a user or post is deleted, all associated comments will also be deleted.
In summary, the rschema_0382 database schema is designed to manage user data, post data, and user-post comments in a social media platform.
gold_question: This is a photo sharing application system. For user management, the system supports users to register and log in using username and password. Users can modify their personal information and avatar, including name, gender, age, occupation, interests, personal profile, etc. For post management, users can publish photo posts with title, description and images, and can view and manage their own posts. For comment management, the system supports users to post and view comments under posts, recording comment time and content, and users can manage their own comments.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0382
CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `occupation` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `personal_profile` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `gender` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `interests` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `post` (
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text NOT NULL,
  `image_url` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `post_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `user_post_comment` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `comment_content` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`, `post_id`, `comment_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `user_post_comment_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `user_post_comment_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `post` (`post_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
